plan.contextChunk: This figure presents the mass spectrum of chloroethane as a bar-line plot on a pale beige field. The vertical axis reads "Relative abundance (%)" and runs from 0 to 100 with labeled ticks every 20 units; the horizontal axis, labeled "m/z" and followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, spans 10 to 70 with tick marks every 5 units. Inline text near the top center identifies the sample as "CH3CH2Cl" with "MW = 64.5". Each ion is drawn as a thin vertical line whose height encodes its abundance. The densest group sits between about 25 and 30, where three tall lines rise to just above 90 percent and to roughly 85 and 75 percent, with shorter lines beside them and a small cluster near 35 to 37. A medium line near 49 reaches about 25 percent, with a shorter one near 51. At the far right a line at 64 climbs to the full 100 percent and carries the label "M (64)", while a line at 66 reaching about 30 percent is labeled "M + 2"; several short lines fall between 62 and 65. Setting those two labeled lines side by side lets the reader take their height ratio directly, roughly three to one — the signature of an element present as two isotopes in that natural abundance.

interactions.teaches: Peak position along the m/z axis identifies the mass of a specific ion, while peak height encodes its relative abundance (how frequently that ion is produced); dimming the neighbors isolates the single stick being read.

The M and M+2 molecular-ion peaks at 64 and 66 form a paired doublet whose height ratio of roughly 3:1 is the diagnostic signature of one chlorine atom, reflecting the natural ³⁵Cl:³⁷Cl isotope abundance.

demo_steps.title: Reading the spectrum
demo_steps.narration: The horizontal axis is mass-to-charge (m/z) and the vertical axis is relative abundance, so every vertical stick is one ion: where it sits gives its mass and how tall it is gives how often it appears. The tallest stick (m/z 64) is defined as 100%.

demo_steps.title: Probe a fragment
demo_steps.narration: Hover any stick to read its exact m/z and abundance while the others dim. The dense cluster near m/z 27-29 is the ethyl-cation fragment family left behind after chlorine departs, showing how fragmentation reveals structure.

demo_steps.title: Spot the chlorine signature
demo_steps.narration: Click the M (64) or M + 2 peak to bracket the molecular-ion doublet. Their heights stand in about a 3:1 ratio — the unmistakable isotopic fingerprint of a single chlorine atom (³⁵Cl vs ³⁷Cl).

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A mass spectrum is read on two channels at once — position gives an ion's mass and height gives its abundance — and an M : M+2 doublet in a ~3:1 ratio is the tell-tale mark of one chlorine atom in the molecule.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Render as a stick spectrum: thin black vertical lines on a pale beige field, not wide bars. Y-axis 'Relative abundance (%)' 0-100 with gridline ticks every 20; X-axis 'm/z' 10-70 with ticks every 5 and a short magenta arrow pointing right after the label. Place 'CH3CH2Cl / MW = 64.5' as plain text near the top center. Reproduce the characteristic peak pattern: a tall tight cluster around m/z 26-30 (peaks ~28/75/91/85%), a low cluster at 35-37, a medium peak ~25% at 49 with a small one at 51, a few short sticks at 62-65, then the dominant M stick at 64 (100%) labeled 'M (64)' and the M+2 stick at 66 (~30%) labeled 'M + 2'. On hover, dim all other sticks and show a small tooltip with that stick's m/z and %; on click of either molecular-ion stick, draw a bracket over the 64/66 pair with a '~3 : 1' label to make the chlorine isotope ratio explicit. Keep the M and M+2 labels in italic serif math styling as in the source.

authoredContext:
The fact that some elements have two common isotopes gives their mass spectra a distinctive appearance. Chlorine, for example, exists as two isotopes, 35Cl and 37Cl, in roughly a 3: 1 ratio. In a sample of chloroethane, three out of four molecules contain a 35Cl atom and one out of four has a 37Cl atom. In the mass spectrum of chloroethane (the figure we see the molecular ion (M) at m/z = 64 for ions that contain a 35Cl and another peak at m/z = 66, called the M + 2 peak, for ions containing a 37Cl. The ratio of the relative abundance of M: M + 2 is about 3: 1, a reflection of the isotopic abundances of chlorine.

Mass spectrum of chloroethane.

The mass spectrum of chloroethane with two peaks at m / z 64 and 66, labeled M and M + 2, on a 3 to 1 height ratio.

In the case of bromine, the isotopic distribution is 50.7% 79Br and 49.3% 81Br. In the mass spectrum of 1-bromohexane (the figure) the molecular ion appears at m/z = 164 for 79Br-containing ions and the M + 2 peak is at m/z = 166 for 81Br-containing ions. The ions at m/z = 135 and 137 are informative as well. The two nearly equally large peaks tell us that the ions at those m/z values still contain the bromine atom. The peak at m/z = 85, on the other hand, does not contain bromine because there is not a large peak at m/z = 87.

discrepancies: The source spectrum is enclosed in a full rectangular frame (a top border line at 100% and a right border line); the generated Chart.js figure draws only the left and bottom axis borders, so the top and right frame lines are missing.

In the source the 'M + 2' annotation sits flush against the right margin at the height of the 66 peak; the generated version floats it just right of the 66 stick, slightly changing its anchoring relative to the plot edge.

The source's three tallest fragment sticks (m/z 27, 28, 29) read as a tight triplet with 28 tallest; the generated sticks reproduce the heights but the 2 px bar thickness makes the triplet spacing look marginally wider than the source's near-touching lines.
evaluation.notes: A highly faithful mass-spectrum reproduction: correct m/z 10-70 and 0-100% axes, beige top-to-bottom gradient, accurate stick positions/heights (28~91, 29~85, 27~75, 49~25, M=100, M+2=30), and all key labels (CH3CH2Cl, MW=64.5, M(64), M+2, magenta m/z arrow) in matching style; hover-probe, click-to-bracket Cl doublet, and a 3-step narration player are all functional and pedagogically on-point, with the only notable visual gap being the missing top/right frame lines of the source's box.
action_items: Draw the top border line at y=100 and the right border line to recreate the source's full rectangular plot frame (e.g. in the annot plugin's afterDraw, stroke a rectangle around chartArea).
Anchor the 'M + 2' label to the right plot margin at the 66-peak height to match the source's edge placement.
Optionally reduce bar spacing / increase bar thickness slightly so the m/z 27-29 triplet reads as tightly clustered as in the source.
